analysis.name: Staci Avery
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lab was very easy, you just have to show up and follow the protocols. Attendance is mandatory and graded on it's own so try to find another section to attend if you can't make it one week there's usually a class ahead and one behind. Grading depends on your TA but for mine you could fix incorrect answers. Only negative was protocols are outdated.

Her class is so low stress and really easy to get an A in. However, she is so ridiculously strict about the attendance policy. My grandmother passed away an hour before the first day of class and she told me that I would be docked points for not attending. Otherwise she is wonderful but be wary that she will not make exceptions for emergencies.

There are two classes taught at the same time: one by Dr. Avery and one by a T/A. You can email her to ask which one she teaches and enroll in that section. Dr. Avery is AWESOME. She is knowledgeable and explains concepts exceptionally well; also, she went out of her way to ensure we had all the supplies we needed to succeed. Labs can be corrected.

Professor Avery is always willing to help students. During lab, she was especially helpful when the class was unsure of protocols or equations. For class assignments, she keeps expectations aligned with a one-credit course, making the workload manageable.

Bio 241 is mostly TA lead, but Professor Avery does come occasionally. She's super nice! She really wants us to succeed. The class is well organized and she provides everything needed for student success.

analysis.name: April Dean
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The homework and everything was easy, but it didn't translate whatsoever to the tests. I spent so much time reading and studying compared to all my other classes like marketing and information systems. Still got the worst grade I will ever get. Get ready to memorize the textbook and then get tested on something completely different.

Her study guides do not cover everything that will be on the test. This is because her tests are super specific and questions could be on literally any sentence from the textbook rather than testing main ideas. I would recommend not taking this class from this professor.

Professor Dean is the sweetest lady, but not a very good professor. I just read the textbook and only went to class during review days because the lectures were not helpful. There are a couple assignments that are very specific with what you need to do, but they are easy. Don't take this class if you are a nutrition major.

Prof Dean is like an old relief society president who went online and got a fake degree. She forgets everything, has to ask her class for answers, and teaches you something wrong at least once a lecture. During the anorexia and other eating disorders lecture, she made lots of insensitive comments and jokes. Also makes the TA answer all questions.

Not a great professor.  She is a nice lady, but doesn't know how to teach or control a classroom.  She would start the lecture and no one would even know because we were all already talking and tuning her out.  I stopped going to class because I could get more done on my own during that time.  Just go to the in class reviews which are graded.

analysis.name: Amanda Smith
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 123 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Never written a review of a professor before, but Pro. Smith was so awesome that I am writing this review. Most reviews you see are for extra credit and below the A grade. Not me, the extra credit deadline expired.  Don't worry she will help you a lot with your essays if you just ask! The class is also super enjoyable (attendance is super required)

Everything we did in class mattered. Lectures were fun and engaging. Essays were free choice, with an emphasis on what we care about rather than a chosen prompt. Mrs. Smith will also work one on one with you and provide you with many opportunities to improve in her class. She has been one of my favorite teachers. I wholeheartedly recommend her.

I absolutely recommend taking this class! Super helpful and caring and the lectures are very engaging. Class has a few major assignments that take a lot of work but it's all doable and no tests. One thing to look out for is the late work policy. Didn't know that early enough so my grade took some hits. But would definitely take this class again.

Mrs. Smith is an amazing teacher who works one-on-one with students and really cares about their learning and development. She teaches in a funny style that helps you remember the course material. She gives enough time to do assignments and allows peer reviews within the classroom setting. I would totally take her class again and recommend it.

Professor Smith was an amazing teacher especially in my place as a freshman. She has set a standard for all my future teachers. Professor Smith makes sure that everyone is clear on the subject and what is being taught. She also creates a safe space that makes it easy to be open and express how you feel towards writing itself and other content.

analysis.name: Matthew Asplund
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 112 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is so smart and really knows chemistry but his lectures can be confusing and he doesn't really teach to the tests. I relied heavily on the TAs and they taught me more than Asplund. Be ready to work hard.

Incredibly homework heavy, especially since he does not really teach anything. Tests were created to fool students, including unknown concepts, and multiple reminders that "I'm going to try to trick you on this". Zero concern for students. Lectures were useless, and he would rather play the cello than spend time explaining things in a rational way.

Hardest class I've had. His lectures weren't my favorite and I didn't think they helped me much. Homework is math based, but exams were conceptual based which was challenging for me. He is very forgiving on exams which was lifesaving. He is a very nice guy and is helpful in office hours so go to those. If you put in the effort, it's a doable class.

Well I never actually met or saw Dr.Asplund so I can't say much about him. In 107, a TA runs the whole class & all the course content was created years ago by someone named Rebecca Sansom. Lowkey the class was confusing and required so much of your time for only 1 credit hour. There's really no easy way out of this class but the TA's got your back!

He has no mercy for his students. The week before finals included a homework assignment (8-12 hours), midterm (4 hours) and group project (easily 8 hours/problem). His lectures are focused on deriving the math of Pchem, but he never shows you how to use the equations. DO NOT GET THE EBOOK! The equations are unreadable and he did nothing to fix it.

analysis.name: Aleksandr Mosenkov
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mosenkov is definitely a great professor; he is extremely caring and is willing to work with you. My only beef is the homework problems' difficulty: some homework problems are really easy and others are obnoxiously hard. Overall, he is great.

Don't be put off by the amount of work and depth of understanding he wants from you. This class is so jam packed with extra credit that you can easily get an A even bombing two tests. Exemplary teacher always incorporating all of BYU's aims and bringing the gospel to the table. If you're unsure, trust me YOU'LL BE FINE!

Dr. Mosenkov has one of the most organized and thought-out class and assignment structures I have ever seen! He really cares about his students and will go out of his way to help if you express any need whatsoever.

Sure he has an accent so it can be hard to understand, sure there is a ton of material, but given the extra credit, and how utterly dedicated he is to your success, its impossible to not get an A. I bombed things and failed an exam and ended up with an A because he is on your side THAT much. Love him. Don't understand the complainers

Extremely organized on learning Suite and in general. Gives so many extra credit opportunities, its impossible to get a bad grade. It might seem like a lot of work because he's passionate about your learning, and wants you to go the extra mile, but really the tests are lightwork and if you pay attention to lectures, you will be more than fine.

analysis.name: Doug Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing! I feel like I won the lottery with this professor. It was difficult and stretching, but Professor Atkinson took any stress away from it. The class is so organized and expectations are super clear. There are so many resources available to help. I was really scared for POLI 300, but it turned out to be nothing but helpful and doable.

Professor Atkinson cares deeply about the material! He put a lot of effort into the class, because it was his first time teaching 300. We gave him some grace as he worked through the first run, and he returned that same understanding to us. My favorite part about Atkinson is that he was actually human, and he cared about my success individually.

He wants you to succeed and is known for being a too lenient grader. He does not like to use technology and doesn't know how to use learning suite that well. I took this class as a freshman but I should have waited to take it until after poli 200 mb. Lectures were interesting but hard to follow which topics we were on because of the disorganization

Dr. Atkinson is a nice guy, but your time is better spent in a different IR class - this is my least favorite one I've taken during my time here. He was unorganized and I felt that lectures could have been way more engaging. Tests were arbitrary. He refuses to use Learning Suite which was just annoying. Class felt like a waste of time.

Very little things graded and doesn't use the traditional routes like LS. A little awkward lectures but is very excited to teach. Asks for people to attend office hours often, so try to do that. I honestly would take him again, but maybe not my first pick just because I enjoy more structured courses.

analysis.name: Alex Lee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took this in summer term, so we had two full-length lectures every class separated by a short break in the middle. He told a math fun fact everyday, was super understanding about deadlines and when you could take tests. He's a grad student and he makes a lot of dad jokes, overall he's pretty great
Alex is the goat. Easily the best math professor I have had. He is super caring and knowledgeable! Definitely take any class from him!

Admittedly, Alex was a TA for my section, but he was SO GOOD, I consider him to have been my professor.  Alex is the most clear and kind math teacher I have ever had.  He's taught me a love for the beauty of mathematics through proofs.  He is extremely flexible with hours and will not leave until all your questions are answered.  He's a can't-miss!

Alex is great! I've taken a quite a few math classes at BYU, and he probably one of my teachers so far. He's knowledgable about the topics, gives great examples, and makes the material very accessible. Calc 2 can be intimidating, but Alex is always encouraging and eager to see all of succeed.

analysis.name: Adam Dynes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Okay so Dynes is so bad at explaining concepts. But he also tells you to contact him if you need to figure something out, but he is so bad at responding to you! I had to figure out a time to meet with him about our papers (a mandatory meeting we all had to do) and I sent him four emails with no reply! To the email he provided to us. So annoying.

Professor Dynes is tough. Does not know how to teach material to his students. His teaching style was ineffective, as reflected in the test scores of almost all the students in our class. Don't take this class with him unless you are ready to put in the work outside of the class. A lot of people would ask him questions and he could not answer them

Prof Dynes is a nice guy, he knows what he's talking about most of the time, but isn't good at explaining it. He's one of those "knows things but doesn't know how to teach those things" guy. You get loads of reading for homework and have to teach yourself. He's also a way tough grader which is too bad since he doesn't teach you well enough for that

Professor Dynes is super smart, and while his lectures can be scattered at times he really emphasizes what you need to know. His reading quizzes can be challenging but he is a fair grader on those and the papers/tests. He also seeks out constructive feedback to try and make the class better which is something many profs don't do. Rewarding class.

Dynes was honestly not a great lecturer in the sense that he is super unorganized and doesn't really have concrete lessons. He goes over time a lot and has to pick it up the next day. He's a tough grader, and he doesn't offer really any extra credit. I recommend doing all the reading and taking thorough notes in lectures, especially for the final.

analysis.name: Ron Wilkinson
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: There wasn't really much interaction between him and the class, since it was an online class. He did make the grading criteria super clear and didn't grade harshly if your speeches were in the criteria. There were quite a few opportunities for extra credit. There also weren't any tests, just 5 speeches that you had to record. Overall, an easy class

There wasn't much interaction between him and the class, since it was an online class. He did make the grading criteria super clear and didn't grade harshly if your speeches were in the criteria. There were quite a few opportunities for extra credit. There also weren't any tests, just 5 speeches that you had to record. Overall, an easy class

Professor Wilkinson structured this class very well! There is a lot of material and criteria to include in your speeches, but it wasn't bad. The material/assignments are easily accessed through canvas. He gives valuable feedback that helps you know what to change in order to receive more credit in future speeches as part of the class.

This class is clear with its assignments. Most week, the assignments include a speech recorded with clear criteria, 10 peer comments with specific criteria on a correct review, and a self-reflection. The class doesn't carry a lot of assignments or tests, but the grading is definitely tough and specific.

Professor Wilkinson was an amazing professor. He was very quick to respond to any questions I had and was very willing to help me succeed. He gave great and specific feedback on my speeches which I really appreciated. Focused heavily on the speeches which I loved because it was a public speaking class.

analysis.name: Scott Bergeson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 238 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I dreaded Physical Science before the semester started; I never would have guessed it would end up being my favorite class! I really appreciate how this class broadened my understanding of science and how the material was clear, but also challenged my mind. I learned a lot, I laughed a lot (like, a LOT), and I'm really going to miss this class.

I like him as a person, but his teaching style does not work for an online class. He would rarely explain the concepts we needed to know and just do examples instead. He would go through the examples so quickly that no one would have the chance to ask questions. With 500 people in the class, even the army of TA's wasn't enough to get help ever.

Prof Bergeson is a great guy and loves what he does but his teaching is geared towards those who already have a knowledge of physics. The tests are very hard and so is the homework. I often met with TA's and I was very accountable and in charge of my learning. I'm not a freshman who's 18 and just came out of highschool. This is a hard class.

Dr. Bergeson is the best physics professor! He will make you work a bit for an A, but come on it is physics!  As far as grading goes he is one of the most fair teachers I have ever met. If you know how to do all the homework you will do fine on the tests! If you are looking to take physics at BYU take it from this guy!

Dr. Bergeson is so kind to his students--you can tell he loves what he does. Lots of tests in 105. We basically took a short midterm every two weeks, which was nice because a single test wouldn't tank your grade. Engaging lectures and really nice lecture slides for studying. His tests are all super fair and I thought his final was very reasonable.

analysis.name: Samond Byun Bishara
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bishara is literally the best. I took his class last semester, and we had a lot of fun. He is not a hard grader at all; many assignments dropped at the end of the semester anyway. I don't know if I learned as much ASL as I should have, but I learned what I wanted and more! Take ASL 101 with him 100%.

He is the sweetest! He is very patient and understanding. Very willing to repeat things or go over something again. He grades really easy and just cares that you are there and you participate. He brought treats for us several times, and we always got to go early.

Attendance is mandatory but needed to practice. He wants students to improve and to do well so he is helpful.  Do ALL of the reading for quizzes and fill out the study guide for tests.  If you do the presentations, activities, and reading you will be fine!

Samond is the best! He is Deaf, so this is definitely an immersion course. He brought us treats a lot and was super accommodating with assignments. One not-so-great thing is he canceled or didn't show up to class around 20 times in the sem with little to no notice. Still tho, my favorite class by far!! 100% recommend!

Samond is the best "language" teacher I've had at BYU (I took both Spanish and French previously). He's deaf, so you really learn to sign. He makes it fun and interactive to the point that I actually WANT to learn more ASL, unlike some other language classes I took. If you go to class, participate, and do the HW, you'll pass the tests & have fun!

analysis.name: Brian Poole
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 160 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Poole is the man. I'd take all my bio classes from him if possible, because 1) he explains things so well and 2) he sounds like Patrick from Spongebob. Enough said.

I was scared of this class but it is actually super manageable. If you listen and take notes in class on the stuff that he says that's NOT on the slides, and then later combine that with the slides into the objectives, you're golden for exams. Dr. Poole also comes up with a lot of demonstrations that help explain and reinforce difficult concepts.

Dr. Poole is the goat. His lectures are pretty entertaining. He is a funny and a kind of awkward guy. His tests aren't bad. The final was the easiest test of them all. He bases them off of the learning objectives so they are pretty easy to study for. He uploads videos of the lectures to Learning Suite. An A is very doable

I LOVED Dr. Poole. He made molecular biology engaging for me, he's super energetic and explains things so well, as well as records lectures. His tests aren't unpredictable, and homework is completion based. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Poole for anyone needing to take MMBIO 240.

Dr. Poole is the best! This was one of my favorite classes by far, he made all of his lectures super engaging and easy to follow and explained difficult infection pathways clearly. He's very clear on what's on the final and what you're expected to know. He's also really funny. I wouldn't recommend skipping class because there's some vital stuff.

analysis.name: Brad Taylor
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 114 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Brother Taylor is the most kind, caring, and loving teacher there is! If  his REL-C class was applicable for me again, I would 100%take his class again! There were so many times where I needed help with getting work done and he let me come to his office to work on my work! His classes were the best and didn't require much other work! He's the best!

The Taylors were amazing! This has been my favorite religion class at BYU because they brought the Spirit to every class. They are so qualified to teach Mission Prep and their experience and knowledge shows. Good amount of homework, but it is necessary for getting prepared for a mission. But above all, they teach with the Spirit which is inspiring!

I LOVED THE TAYLORS!!! They are truly the nicest people ever, I see Christ light in them every class and they truly care about you. The work is not hard and is more for your progress and preparation. I'm so glad I took this class before my mission, it was very eye opening for what I will be doing on my mission. I learned so many interesting things!

Brother and Sister Taylor are AMAZING! Their class is so uplifting and just all around fun to be in! There are BOM readings due before each class, but they are so enriching and wonderful. Truly mission prep has been so helpful and this class, a blessing in my life. Easy, fun class and a good one if you're torn about serving a mission/going on one!

Brother Taylor teaches this course with his wife, Sister Taylor. They are amazing! Its super easy, but you do only get 2 absences if you want an A. Other than that, I loved it. They both served missions when they were young and they were mission presidents in Korea. They have great stories and they care about their students. 10/10 would take again.

analysis.name: Brett Pickett
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I'm gonna be honest here, he's a chill guy but this class is worse than losing my first wife. This class is horrid, bro made the test closed note which is fine but the class is not set up for closed note exams. The TA's are not ballers like they should be. Do not take this class if you wanna be happy and get ragebaited by this class.

BE WARNED: The high ratings are from when his tests were open note. This semester, all tests are closed note, but he is using the exact same exams as before. They are unfairly difficult and not designed to be taken from memory.
His lectures are a waste of time. Slides are a confusing word salad and he just makes jokes instead of teaching. AVOID!

He is a great guy but my experience was that this class was made to be harder than it should have been. It was hard to identify what was important information from the slides and lectures, and how to apply it for the tests and quizzes. Really nice guy though and will work with you if you need it.

The class is poorly designed. Dr. Pickett is a nice person, but the class structure isn't designed for the success of his students. Between the way he lectures, the slides provided, and difficulty of the tests (and lack of study material to help) makes the class frustrating.

If you do anything in this life, don't take this class. Man, this year was tough, no matter how much time you put into this class, it'll never be enough for an A. I didn't have any fun this year cause I was studying for this class. I can't tell you how much this class consumed me and made things impossible. Idk if ill ever recover from this class.

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I took Dr. Griffin for Bio 220 and it was hard but not terrible. Ecology has been a nightmare. Easy material. Tons of busy work (weekly homework, writings, class discussions, etc.). Tests are extremely difficult and Im a 4.0 student. They are poorly written (lots of mistakes, very guess what Im thinking). 94 for an A. Avoid at all costs.

He loves his subject, but he kind of treats you like you are dumb. I used to ask lots of questions, but he just treated me like an idiot in class. He has a hard time with anyone having a different perspective than his. I took him for both bio 220 and bio 350.. he was ruder in bio 350. His tests are "guess what I am thinking".

I really like Professor Griffen as a person, however not so much as a teacher. He was good at keeping class interesting, however when it came to tests it was hard to know what he was looking for at times. Some questions were just plainly poorly written. Very strict on late work, and you have to read the book before each class to do well.

Dr. Griffen is the best! He knows so much and there can be a lot of info in lecture, but if you pay attention are willing to think critically the tests are manageable. Exams are open note so he mostly tests application. The homework assignments build into a research proposal which was interesting.

Burnt out senior signing off here, and I have nothing but good things to say about Dr. Griffen. Yes the tests are difficult, yes there is a lot of content, but if you can make an argument that stands on its own you will do just fine. Not at all a copy and paste professor, will expect you to think. Wish he ran the whole biology department.

Everyday was a random discussion of things we have already talked about and talking to us like Elementary school kids. Brandon was a good person but I dreaded going to his class. He treated us like we were elementary schoolers and not in the cute fun way other professors do. I think overall the course from him was good. I will say that whenever I asked a question his response was usually, "That's not an easy answer." Professor McMillan is super nice and cares about his students. He gives good lectures and he wants to see us succeed. There aren't many things graded, so you really have to do well on all of them to succeed. Grading can take weeks, but overall it's not a bad class.

Lots of essays writing.  Class felt pretty unorganized with assignment descriptions on PowerPoints, syllabus, or just given in class.  No serious tests.  Great professor but lectures do get long in the evenings.  Just make sure to have him review bigger assignments before final submissions. Attendance is mandatory (in SLC Center).
Great guy! Class was easy and there weren't many assignments. He is very understanding and willing to work with you on things. Worth taking in SL over BYU campus.

By far the best religion class I have ever taken! Fascinating and engaging, Brother Bolingbroke is an immersive storyteller, and his passion for the scriptures shines through in his lectures. review_highlights.comment: It was an okay class. Dr. Griffiths often said things that were inappropriate and culturally insensitive but he seems like a good guy. Tests were "eh", the material we had to remember was extensive and didn't seem that important.

Brother Griffiths is so funny!! I loved going to his class because I always felt inspired and also got a good laugh. He covered controversial subjects well and allows for a lot of class participation. Assignments (mostly reading quizzes) were straightforward and tests were pretty easy.

The reading is somewhat heavy, but the resources he provides are awesome! I would never had found them in a personal study on my own. You'll find the topics intriguing and the lectures mind-blowing. He has a great sense of humor and delivers the lectures really well. He offers lots of opportunities for extra credit and study helps for the tests.

Brother Griffiths is the best! He has a great sense of humor, which he incorporates into lectures. However, we talk about some serious subjects in this class and he has a very appropriate manner. There are three tests and reading quizzes before each class. There's a big term paper and two smaller papers, but all are manageable. Would take again!

He is amazing. Best religion professor I've had at BYU. The class isn't very hard and you aren't bored to death in class because the man is a stand-up comedian. Never in my life have I recommended a religion prof until today. LET IT BE HEARD LADIES AND GENTS.

analysis.name: Christopher Hodson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really respect Professor Hodson, he's very well-versed in what he teaches. The two midterms and final are pretty much the only things going into your grade, so that can be tough. But honestly, I never read the textbook and maybe showed up to 50% of the lectures and got A- on the midterms and an A on the final, so it's not bad. He's a cool guy.

Lots of reading but not too bad if you schedule it out. I'm a 4.0 student and the content was not difficult at all. The average scores on the tests were ~80% and then for the big essay ~93%. Class is very doable and Dr. Hodson won't be your problem if you struggling to get a good grade. Just pay attention in class, and do the reading and you got it

Best professor I have every had in my life!!!!!! It's not even that hard either, the reading is way fun, and he is seriously the BEST lecturer in the world. Seriously my favorite professor at BYU so far. analysis.name: Cougar Hall

Coug is a great guy, really enjoyed taking this class from him. Not very difficult of a class either. Only complaint is that lectures felt a little rambly at times, but overall really enjoyed this class. He's a great guy.

Cougar is awesome and cares about his students. HLTH383 was a course that I think everyone should take. It's an easy A, but more than anything the content is so interesting and applicable. Cougar teaches in such a relaxing and chill way that makes you want to be in class. Whether you need it or you want an elective, it's def a worthwhile class.

analysis.name: David Calabro

He is a nice professor. He is clearly passionate about his areas of study and will occasionally go down a random tangent. He cares about each individual student and wants them to succeed. Bro. Calabro is really nice and learns almost every students name. He really loves history and adds lots of ancient history into the class. Lectures can be a little boring but tests and homework are very easy.

Professor Hawkins is such a caring man. He will work with you because he understands. He made UNIV such a lovely experience because he really worked to make it meaningful. He's so funny and such a joy to be around. Take UNIV from him if you actually want to get something out of it.

Dr. B. was my favorite professor...class wasn't too hard and I really liked attending his lectures. Highly recommend

review_highlights.comment: This class was absolutely horrible. While the professor was very kind and willing to give out extension, his teaching style was impossible to follow. Attending his class was pointless since he was hard to follow and the book was just as bad. I had to find a tutor who was willing to just act as my teacher. Do NOT choose a class with Ouyang.

By far the worst instructor I've ever had at BYU.  I'm a pretty positive guy, but this guy was horrible.  41 people at the beginning of the semester, at the end only 15-18 were coming.  I've never failed a class, but I'm probably going to fail this one.  It's not worth taking from him, and if you do, it's not worth even worth going to class.

The course material is difficult as it is, and taking it from Ouyang doesn't help that. Aside from his accent, he often makes assumptions that you know things you may not, and the lectures aren't very interesting. They still can be helpful, though! If you read the chapter before the lecture, then the lectures become less of a waste of time.

You often leave his class feeling like your time was wasted. I learned more in the math lab than in his classroom. The averages in the class are low, so he has to give a GIANT curve at the end of the semester so everybody gets decent grades. He's got a thick accent too, so he's hard to understand.

Worst teacher ever.  Takes the final and not only do you get 0 points for missing a problem, he also takes away 1/2 point for each one. So much for being on the student's side, so much for helping the student succeed.  And, he lets us know the day of the test through a message on blackboard that he's doing it. He's unclear, unorganized, BADDDDDDDD!

Very respectful individual with insightful classes. I have heard some say his classes are a bit dull, but I had no issues with him, he treated me well and I thought the content was quite interesting and well organized.

review_highlights.comment: Brother Ostler knows a lot about the gospel, but the class is stupidly difficult for 2 credits. There's a weekly study guide with at least 2 talks to read for it, it's hard to take notes in class because he skips around so much and includes LOTS of personal stories, and the tests are mostly "choose all that apply" questions (which I hate).

Super nice guy, knows a lot about the gospel but he just stands up front the whole time and goes on and on and the class does not participate at all. He also requires you to read between 3-8 full length articles or talks before every class period, and more scriptures, then you never talk about it. I would recommend taking it from someone else.

Dr. Ostler is not very clear on how he is grading, what he is talking about, etc. He would often goes off on tangents and I wasn't sure what to take notes on. Study guides due every class were easy but time consuming. I learned some interesting things and he is a nice guy but I would recommend taking it from someone else.

Dr. Ostler was a nice guy, but definitely will not take from him again. He talks about how he wants us to "really learn" but then makes us spend the whole semester chasing down "points" for our grades--very 2nd grade again. Lots of busy work and lectures were completely disorganized. Won't be taking from him again.

LOTS of busy work for every day of class. Study guides for tests are not helpful at all so you're basically on your own for tests. Which are fairly confusing because there are a lot of "select all that apply". For those like me who I am not a good test taker, you don't pass the test or AKA get lower than 60 you "dont get credit" AKA you get a 0

review_highlights.comment: Professor Owen's 321 class is easily the best Japanese course at BYU. He is an amazing instructor, and wants to help you succeed. He shares a perspective of what business is like in Japan, and the coursework he provides is very up-to-date and manageable. This class will make you feel more comfortable with Japanese discussions & presentations.

Professor Owen's class is very well structured, in a way that you are not drowning with work but are given a couple assignments per week that allow efficient and effective learning. He selects articles on current events in Japan that are discussed as a class each week. The environment is very safe and comfortable. I loved and enjoyed this class!

This was by far my favorite Japanese class I've taken and it's thanks to Owen Sensei. Although he teaches on the side and has a different job as his main career, he puts a lot of work into his class and students. Pretty easy as long as you participate but you still learn so much stuff that is actually applicable to real life Japanese conversations.

Owen Sensei was my favorite Japanese professor I've had. He is a new prof, but has used Japanese in his business for years and comes from a cool business perspective. He is very organized, sets clear expectations for grades. I learned more in his class vs others bc he focuses on letting us speak and repeats kanji on quizzes. I would def recommend.

This was my favorite Japanese class at BYU. Owen Sensei made it a great experience. Instead of having to read ancient articles we were allowed to choose applicable topics and current events. He teaches real life business skills that apply to all majors. Owen sensei pushed us to work hard but also created a safe space to make mistakes and improve.

Professor Owens truly cares about his students. There is quite a bit of reading, but I found a lot of it to be very interesting. He also allows midterm appeals which is really nice. I loved his lectures and he is just such a sweet guy!

I thought the reviews on here were misleading. He's a super nice guy who actually learns everybody's name in the class....impressive. Profe Oveson is sss th booomb. He's  got a wicked sense a humor ya might havfta get used to but it makes life fun. He's awesome w tests gave us some extra points, good feedback on oral exams. Take this class if you love psychology and if you are ready to learn a lot!! You must read the textbook!!

Very well-qualified to teach this course. Caring and attentive to questions or concerns. He made long lectures fun with engaging videos and you could tell he knew the material very well. Highly recommend Prof. Steffen.

This class was pretty easy. I didn't pay much attention to lectures or keep up with the reading and still got an A. Just watch the review sessions and study the guide—that's all you really need. Dr. Steffen's lectures are somewhat boring but attendance is graded daily. There are three 4-6 page papers, three exams (in testing center), weekly timed textbook quizzes, and a final class presentation. I recommend reading the chapters of the textbook because this will be the best preparation for exams. Overall, lighter class work than most.

He does usually teach higher level classes, so if you ask a question he has a tendency to make you feel really dumb, no matter the question. Very fast lectures.

His class inspired me to jump off the pre-med boat and pursue research even though I'm pretty stubborn when it comes to life decisions. He knows his stuff but is not good at coming down to your level of not as advanced thinking. Dr. Patterson knows his stuff. 462 is just a hard class. Often, the lectures didn't seem to relate to any homework problems or test questions, so it was sometimes hard to pay attention knowing that. I enjoy chemistry but Dr. Savage made it really hard.  Compared to other teachers, there is less structure, and in my opinion, he doesn't prep you well for tests or the ACS.

By far my hardest but also favorite class taken at BYU! He has a problem set and quiz due every Friday, but both are easy to get full points on if you study and visit the TA lab or office hours for any questions you have. Tests felt a bit harder than weekly assignments, but if you study hard and are able to understand the concepts you can do great!

He is pretty darn good at lectures. The only problem I had with him was that he expects you to read his mind. If you don't use the exact wording he wants then you won't get the points even when your explanation is SPOT ON. On my 1st exam the TA put "too long" on my explanation, then I got docked for being too concise on the 2nd. Truly savage!

He is a nice guy but I hated the content of this class. Lots of work for a one credit. The TAs were the most unhelpful.

Professor Rich was really nice, and super easy to contact out of class. review_highlights.comment: Professor Jenkins runs an exceptionally well-designed course. Content is learned at home through videos, while class time is used for practice and clarification. Dr. Jenkins is so nice and his lectures are very interesting. There are weekly quizzes (they are pretty easy), 2 midterms, and then the final. Class is spent applying what you learned into real world applications. Grades are based entirely on quizzes, but they are easy. Honestly learned the material better and easier than other professors.

There is no proctoring on quizzes or exams, so if you get tempted to cheat and have a heavy guilt complex, this class isn't for you. If you watch the videos and take good notes, you don't need to go to class. I liked going because he would review test and quiz questions. analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Liu is the best Chinese professor at BYU. She genuinely cares for all of her students individually and wants them to love learning Chinese. Sometimes homework is a bit overwhelming, and there are lots of tests, but Liu laoshi is incredibly understanding and flexible. I learned so much from her!

Liu Laoshi is amazing! Our class was mixed RMs and non-RMs but she was fair with grading to your level. Her lectures were informative and funny. The test review sheets were extremely clear about exactly what to prepare for. Definitely improved my Chinese ability.

Liu Laoshi is hands down the best professor I've had at BYU to this point. Every class period I felt like I was learning so much. She was so inspiring and the layout of the class was so organized that I felt I would have to try hard to not get an A. She cares so much about all of her students and about teaching and it reflects in each class.

At first, Liu Laoshi seemed really strict and mean.  But after a week or so, she opened up and you could see that she really cares about her students.  She is easily my favorite Chinese teacher at BYU so far.  She has a great passion for teaching the language and is an expert teacher.  She manages class time very well. Tests not that bad.

I loved this class. There is quite a bit of homework, but none of the homework is fluff work. Liu laoshi is also really helpful-she truly cares about each student individually. She noticed my tones were often off, so she helped me make an individualized plan and extra materials to help improve them.

analysis.name: Bruce Young
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Okay, let me start this off by saying Professor Young is THE NICEST guy. But he shouldn't be teaching this course. Our first test  included 32 authors and 62 works. I made my own 15-page study guide and I'll still be lucky to get above a 70% on the test. There's a ton of reading for each class (2+ hours) and he doesn't drop the count for projects.

Professor Young is a great guy, but I hated his class. He makes you read 3+ hours of literature for every class period, and he expects you to remember ALL OF IT. The tests are absurd; he expects you to remember everything from the 2000+ pages you read. Don't take his class unless you read fast and have an exceptional retention rate.

While everything is posted, youll quickly realize that this does not help. Classes are filled with boring lectures that barely cover anything on what you read and the papers due have very loose guidelines. However, even with a well reviewed paper, its hard to get a good grade. Tests in this class are a nightmare with lots of things to memorize.
A teacher who doesn't really know how to teach.  Great guy, but horrible teacher.  So much reading!  I was really excited to take this class, but after I started it, I dreaded going.

While I enjoyed the readings and sometimes the lectures, I found that the exams have very strict guidelines and sometimes the "right" answer doesn't actually count for full credit. He offers a "review" paper the day before an exam (though they are posted online) and everything on that paper (and more) will be covered on the exam.

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zabriskie is the biggest fishing fanatic I have ever seen! When I struggled he worked with me one-on-one till I caught something. He wants everyone to succeed.

He is the pillar of EXDM! He wants us to actually learn and internalize the topics we cover. It was a transformational experience for me and I know that I see the world differently because of it. I was never worried about my grade, just put in the effort to actually do the stuff. I had so much fun and made so many friends! Everyone should take this

Dr. Z is awesome!  He's a very energetic teacher and is easy to listen to.  He really cares about his students and is very fair with his students.  There is a lot of work, but it is all very useful and each assignment builds upon the next.  Go to class, pay attention, and do your assignment and you'll get an A.  START YOUR VOLUNTEERING RIGHT AWAY!

He truly does care about each student wants you to understand the material and succeed. He keeps class fun and interesting with creative ways to teach new ideas! In the intro class, he gives two big projects. One is a group project, and the other is a personal project. I enjoyed both and learned a lot. I highly recommend him!

Dr. Z is one of the best professors at BYU. He has real world experience in the field and has an infectious teaching style that hots every learning style. He has a ton of energy and can't ever stay in one place at a time. He cares deeply about each student and will do whatever he can to help you succeed.

analysis.name: Zachary Boyd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Boyd is a great professor! He knows his stuff and his very willing to help students succeed. His lectures are very clear and easy to understand. There was an online part and a written part for homework. Each part was very doable. Boyd even sometimes will go over a homework problem at the start of class before the homework is due.

The 2 midterms are both 20% of your grade and the final is 25%. The rest of your grade is made up of the daily homework assignments, both online and written. He is an amazing teacher though and really knows how to engage the class.

Dr. Boyd is a brilliant man. He literally creates math to solve problems in various industries. Math 213 is different and it is NOT calculus. The hard part of the class is adopting a new way of thinking. He really helped during office hours with all my questions. He really cared and made sure I understood everything I had questions on.

Professor Boyd is very kind in the way he runs his class. He was reasonable with helping us prep for tests, and genuinely took and answered questions. Not his fault, because all math 213 uses the same webassign, but there were just so many assignments. Be prepared for one assignment a day at least. Overall, GREAT class.

review_highlights.comment: This man is like my soul brother.   I've never had a better professor. He's hilarious, caring, easy to understand. I wish he would teach all of my classes. Attendance is important, but with Professor Chase, you won't want to miss even a second of his lectures-- they're that good.   Be warned: You'll be hooked after the first class.
He deserves all the chili peppers.  Best class I've ever taken.

Professor Chase is determined to ensure that every single student understands the important concepts of what he is teaching. He's a very easy professor to approach and ask questions. He gives very detailed and helpful feedback on papers. His lectures are very easy to understand as well as funny. He can be pretty sarcastic, don't take it personally.
Loved the class. Loved the teacher. Loved the readings. I wish Zach could teach all of my classes. He really gets it. He's also the smartest man I've ever met.

This man understands reading better than anyone else I know. He can point directly to the reading to discuss complicated theorists. He expects students to make accurate connections between theorists, and actually understand the reading. So basically you actually have to learn something to do well in the class. He is great.

analysis.name: Brinley Zabriskie
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zabriskie truly cares about her students. She tried hard to engage and connect with each student. Two pretty big group projects but straightforward on what's required. Homeworks prepare you well for it. Tests are very fair, she doesn't give unnecessarily tough exam questions, review quizzes are an accurate gauge of what the exams will be like.

Dr. Zabriskie has been my favorite statistics professor so far because she focuses on what we need to know as students instead of going on tangents about abstract concepts that are beyond our needs for the course. She gives printouts of powerpoint slides which was super helpful. Tests were challenging but the homework prepared you well for them.

Dr. Z did a great job at catering to the class and making sure to teach for our comprehension. She is great at taking and answering questions. Tests are really hard but if you do the homework and study well you can succeed. Dr. Z is great in her office hours as well and really easy to reach outside of class. One of the best professors I've had

Dr Zabriskie is an excellent teacher and is very student-focused. You will learn a ton if you show up to class and do your homework. She adapts lessons to student's needs. The grading on the R homework, group projects, and tests is extremely meticulous. If you want an A, go overboard on detail on your homework.

Long homework all done in R, but usually more than half of the answers are given in the class codes. Three tests, NON comprehensive. Tests given as a take home in R, and a light multiple choice in the testing center. If you read the notes she gives you there are no tricks, you can get an A.

analysis.name: Timothy Zeidner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Brother Zeidner relies on the Spirit to teach every lesson -- he really cares about the content he is teaching as well as his students. Every week he gives feedback on our responses we right about various activities in Preach my Gospel.  Best part of the class was the Christlike Attributes assignments -- life changing and inspirational.  Take him!!

I LOVED Brother Zeidner's class! I looked forward to it every week. He's a great teacher because he listens to the Spirit and he genuinely cares about his students. There are no tests, but there are weekly papers (which are pretty easy) and monthly papers (which are easy if you stay on top of it). I would take this class again! Take from BROTHER Z!

I LOVE Brother Zeidner. He has been my favorite professor here at BYU. He is so great at inviting the spirit into missionary work and I learned so much from him. He works closely with the missionary department at the MTC, so he really knows his stuff. His assignments are focused on improving you as a missionary and not on busywork. Also, no tests!

Bro Zeidner is an amazing teacher. He works at the MTC and really has wonderful insight. There is a small weekly writing assignment that he reads and gives personal feedback to every week. If you are looking for a professor that will either help you know if you should go on a mission or help steer your preparation, he is your guy. P.S. no tests!

Brother Zeidner is incredible! Class is one big discussion and there is a lot of peer interaction. There is reading and a short assignment each week and he grades off that and attendance-No tests. Our last day of class was at his house. You can feel the love he has for each of his students and the gospel and he really preps you for a mission.

review_highlights.comment: I thought that this class was terrible. Zeb Weeks is by far the worst teacher I have ever had at BYU. Way too much reading and the tests were ridiculously hard. Too much memorization. Lectures were very vauge and hard to follow. I would not recommend him to anyone. He really didn't know how to teach and spent half the class saying "I don't know."

This class had a lot of unrealistically long reading assignments. We were told little about how to write the essays. I was sad that much of class was reading texts out loud that almost no one had read. The quizzes were manageable and tests were fair. The class needed more structure. Lectures were entertaining sometimes. He has a fun personality.

HARD CLASS, hands down i was not ready my first semester at byu to struggle this much with a class. the girls in my class thought he was hot at the beginning, but that changed.  tests were almost impossible. i don't think it is fair to have to memorize part of the aeneid and have to recite it perfectly in front of the class to get a good grade.

This class was really interesting, but I sometimes struggled to keep up with the enormous amount of reading. I know he was actually easier then some on reading, but I was so overwhelmed I found myself making friends with sparknotes alot. But the material was really interesting and Zeb kept the class discussions fun and easy going.

Tons and tons and tons of reading, the exams were misleading as well.  I walked away from a particular test honestly believing i hadn't missed a single question, only to discover i had failed.  his lectures were very interesting, but they didn't make all of the stress, reading and failing worthwhile.  Avoid if you can...

THIS IS THE WORST CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN. DON'T TAKE IT. I was confused 99.9% of the time. She takes all semester to factor in any extra credit work. You'll have no idea what grade you actually have until the end. I'm still kind of bitter about a test I took where she gave me a 77% on an essay even though a fulfilled all the criteria. LAAAAAAAAAAAME

Most disorganized teacher I've ever had. Syllabus was so vague. Dates for tests were always changed and hard to keep track of. She send like four emails a day. Teaches the class like there are 30 students instead of 150. lots of group work. NO CLEAR LECTURES OR INSTRUCTIONS. Do not take this class from this teacher.

Do not take from Dr. Duan.. You can get an A but it will be the most frustrating class you ever take. All of the assignments are extremely confusing and the rubrics are worded very poorly. Dr. Duan is intelligent, has a dry sense of humor and seems like a fair individual; however, I would strongly recommend not taking this class from her. The syllabus does not match with LS and dates are constantly switched. The inconsistency with her slides and teaching is frustrating and confusing. She sends excessive emails. Very disorganized.

review_highlights.comment: I loved the class from Dr Zirker. Its true that the lectures can be boring, but you learn a lot. She cares for her students success and thats all that mattered to me. Each class you have 5 or 6 question quizzes on muscle OIAN and theyre easy pts. Pretty easy class if you can ace the lab tests (easier than PDBIO 220) and study her powerpoints.

Dr. Zirker is awesome, she was able to make lectures a little more interesting because she applied the things she taught clinically. There are so many tests and quizzes it is ridiculous, but if you study her slides, get the lab material down youll do fine. She is always willing to help and is on the students side, take it from her.
Pretty dry lectures. TONS OF QUIZZES. The subject itself has a ton of info, but she doesnt prepare you well for tests. You have to go to TA reviews to get any idea whats going to be on the test.

Professor Zirker is just awesome. Her class is perfect for someone going into physical or occupational therapy. She really wants the students to succeed and will work with them if you go to class and make an effort. If you study right before class for the quizzes and really pay attention in lecture the tests aren't bad!

Professor Zirker is one of my favorite professors at BYU. She is so kind and is excited about what she is teaching. Shes a physical therapist so she knows how to teach applicable anatomy. Overall this was my favorite class Ive ever taken. Its a lot to know but if you have a passion for the material, the work is easy.

review_highlights.comment:
He is one of the most literal people ever. He has a bit of a “god” complex and thinks he is the smarter than everyone but in my experience the best, smartest people understand things so well that they can explain them simply and clearly.

Maybe things were different this semester because we were all online, but please DO NOT take 406 from zimbelman. Audit should be the easiest class your first semester of the junior core, and zimbelman somehow makes the most simple of topics confusing. Professor Zimbelman is a really nice guy. It's obvious he cares about his students and he is quick to reach out when someone is struggling. My problem is with his exams. Zimbelman is hilarious. Audit is by far the easiest class of the first half of the junior core, but it's also super boring. Zimbelman makes class fun and exciting, even if the material is dry. review_highlights.comment: Emilie is arguably the most phenomenal language professor I've ever had.  She's super thorough and helps you reach your potential.  Sounds corny, but she sets high standards and then helps you reach them.  Homework and class attendance are a must, but the course is very well-structured and there are no surprises.  Very willing to help students.

I have never had a teacher at BYU who has been more helpful to me. It wasn't the easiest course for me, and she actually took time to come up to me and ask how she could help. I learned a TON. I was conversational at the end of the semester, and that was with a B in the class. If you're ready to put time in (like 2-3 hours a day), you will get an A

Cares about the students and pushes them to be their best. Her curriculum prepares you for exactly what you need to do- if you do the homework then you will pass the test. She is willing to help anyone that is struggling but has no mercy for complaining or slacking off. Definitely the professor to choose if you are serious about learning Arabic.

Ustaaza Emilie is incredible. Arabic is really hard language to learn, but she gives you all the help you need and will always answer any questions you have. She's very encouraging and really cares about her students. Her class is tough though. Expect a lot of homework, but if you do all of that homework, though, you're sure to get a good grade!

Emilie is incredible! She really knows how to push you to do your best and succeed in learning such a difficult language. Definitely put in at least 2-3 hours of practice per day, she has a knack for knowing when you haven't memorized all the vocab words. This isn't a class you take for fun, you have to work hard, but you get a lot out of it.
